body:
Geometry helps us plan a room, build a garden or wrap a box.

Scale drawings: a map with scale 1 cm : 5 km means every centimeter on the map stands for 5 kilometers.

Circles: the radius r goes from the center to the edge; the diameter d = 2r.
- Circumference: C = πd (or 2πr)
- Area: A = πr²
We use 3.14 for π.

Worked example: a circle has radius 5 cm.
C = 2 × 3.14 × 5 = 31.4 cm
A = 3.14 × 5 × 5 = 78.5 cm²

Angles: complementary angles add to 90°, supplementary angles add to 180°, and vertical angles (across from each other where two lines cross) are equal.

Solids: volume of a prism = area of the base × height. Surface area is the total area of all the faces.

In this unit you will use scale, circles, angles, area and volume to solve real design problems.
title: Measuring Our World
